3	A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.
4	
5	## Features
6	
7	- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
8	- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
9	- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
10	- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
11	- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
12	- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
13	- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage
14	
15	## Installation
16	
17	This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	```go
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25	    "context"
26	    "fmt"
27	    "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"
28	)
29	
30	func main() {
31	    s := scheduler.New()
32	
33	    s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
34	        Name:     "daily-cleanup",
35	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
36	        Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
37	            fmt.Println("Running cleanup...")
38	            return nil
39	        },
40	    })
41	
42	    s.Start()
43	    defer s.Stop(context.Background())
44	
45	    // Keep running...
46	    select {}
47	}
48	```
49	
50	## Cron Expression Format
51	
52	### 5-Field Format (Standard)
53	```
54	┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
55	│ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
56	│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
57	│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
58	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7) (Sunday = 0 or 7)
59	│ │ │ │ │
60	* * * * *
61	```
62	
63	### 6-Field Format (With Seconds)
64	```
65	┌───────────── second (0 - 59)
66	│ ┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
67	│ │ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
68	│ │ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
69	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
70	│ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7)
71	│ │ │ │ │ │
72	* * * * * *
73	```
74	
75	### Special Characters
76	
77	- `*` - Any value (every minute, every hour, etc.)
78	- `,` - List of values: `1,15,30` (1st, 15th, and 30th)
79	- `-` - Range: `9-17` (9 AM through 5 PM)
80	- `/` - Step: `*/15` (every 15 units)
81	
82	### Common Examples
83	
84	| Schedule | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `* * * * *` | Every minute |
87	| `0 * * * *` | Every hour |
88	| `0 0 * * *` | Daily at midnight |
89	| `0 9 * * 1-5` | Weekdays at 9 AM |
90	| `*/15 * * * *` | Every 15 minutes |
91	| `0 0 1 * *` | First day of every month |
92	| `0 0 * * 0` | Every Sunday at midnight |
93	| `30 14 * * *` | Every day at 2:30 PM |
94	
95	## Timezone Support
96	
97	```go
98	// Global timezone for all jobs
99	s := scheduler.New(
100	    scheduler.WithTimezone("America/New_York"),
101	)
102	
103	// Per-job timezone (overrides global)
104	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
105	    Name:     "tokyo-report",
106	    Schedule: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM Tokyo time
107	    Timezone: "Asia/Tokyo",
108	    Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
109	        // Runs at 9 AM in Tokyo
110	        return nil
111	    },
112	})
113	```
114	
115	**Important**: Always use IANA timezone names (`America/New_York`, not `EST`).
116	
117	## Middleware
118	
119	Middleware wraps job handlers to add cross-cutting behavior. Multiple middleware can be chained together.
120	
121	### Built-in Middleware
122	
123	#### Recovery (Panic Handling)
124	
125	```go
126	s := scheduler.New(
127	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
128	        scheduler.Recovery(func(jobName string, r interface{}) {
129	            log.Printf("Job %s panicked: %v", jobName, r)
130	        }),
131	    ),
132	)
133	```
134	
135	#### Logging
136	
137	```go
138	type Logger interface {
139	    Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
140	    Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
141	}
142	
143	s := scheduler.New(
144	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
145	        scheduler.Logging(myLogger),
146	    ),
147	)
148	```
149	
150	#### Timeout
151	
152	```go
153	s := scheduler.New(
154	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
155	        scheduler.Timeout(5 * time.Minute),
156	    ),
157	)
158	```
159	
160	### Combining Middleware
161	
162	```go
163	s := scheduler.New(
164	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
165	        scheduler.Recovery(panicHandler),
166	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
167	        scheduler.Timeout(10 * time.Minute),
168	    ),
169	)
170	```
171	
172	**Order matters**: Middleware are applied left-to-right. In the example above:
173	1. Recovery (outermost) catches panics from everything
174	2. Logging logs the execution
175	3. Timeout (innermost) wraps the actual handler
176	
177	### Custom Middleware
178	
179	```go
180	func Metrics(recorder MetricsRecorder) scheduler.Middleware {
181	    return func(next scheduler.JobHandler) scheduler.JobHandler {
182	        return func(ctx context.Context) error {
183	            start := time.Now()
184	            err := next(ctx)
185	            duration := time.Since(start)
186	
187	            jobName := scheduler.GetJobName(ctx)
188	            recorder.Record(jobName, duration, err)
189	
190	            return err
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	```
195	
196	## Graceful Shutdown
197	
198	Always use `Stop()` with a context to allow jobs to finish cleanly:
199	
200	```go
201	// Give jobs up to 30 seconds to complete
202	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
203	defer cancel()
204	
205	if err := s.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
206	    log.Printf("Shutdown error: %v", err)
207	}
208	```
209	
210	Jobs should respect context cancellation:
211	
212	```go
213	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
214	    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
215	        select {
216	        case <-ctx.Done():
217	            return ctx.Err() // Canceled
218	        default:
219	            // Do work
220	        }
221	    }
222	    return nil
223	}
224	```
225	
226	## Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Always Name Your Jobs
229	
230	Names are used for logging, metrics, and debugging:
231	
232	```go
233	Name: "user-cleanup-job" // Good
234	Name: "job1"             // Bad
235	```
236	
237	### 2. Add Descriptions and Tags
238	
239	```go
240	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
241	    Name:        "stale-session-cleanup",
242	    Description: "Removes user sessions older than 30 days",
243	    Tags:        []string{"maintenance", "security"},
244	    Schedule:    "0 3 * * *",
245	    Handler:     cleanupSessions,
246	})
247	```
248	
249	### 3. Use Appropriate Middleware
250	
251	Always include Recovery and Logging in production:
252	
253	```go
254	scheduler.New(
255	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
256	        scheduler.Recovery(logPanic),
257	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
258	    ),
259	)
260	```
261	
262	### 4. Avoid Scheduling Exactly on the Hour
263	
264	Many systems schedule jobs at `:00`, causing load spikes. Stagger your jobs:
265	
266	```go
267	"5 2 * * *"  // 2:05 AM (good)
268	"0 2 * * *"  // 2:00 AM (often overloaded)
269	```
270	
271	### 5. Make Jobs Idempotent
272	
273	Jobs may run multiple times (crash recovery, etc.). Design them to be safely re-runnable:
274	
275	```go
276	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
277	    // Use unique constraint or check-before-insert
278	    db.Exec("INSERT IGNORE INTO processed_items ...")
279	    return nil
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 6. Handle Timezones Explicitly
284	
285	Always specify timezone for business-hour jobs:
286	
287	```go
288	Timezone: "America/New_York" // Good
289	// Timezone: ""              // Bad (defaults to UTC)
290	```
291	
292	### 7. Test Your Cron Expressions
293	
294	Use a cron expression calculator before deploying:
295	- [crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru/)
296	- Write unit tests with the parser
297	
298	## Testing Jobs
299	
300	Test job handlers independently of the scheduler:
301	
302	```go
303	func TestCleanupJob(t *testing.T) {
304	    ctx := context.Background()
305	
306	    err := cleanupHandler(ctx)
307	    if err != nil {
308	        t.Fatalf("cleanup failed: %v", err)
309	    }
310	
311	    // Verify cleanup occurred
312	}
313	```
314	
315	Test schedule parsing:
316	
317	```go
318	func TestScheduleParsing(t *testing.T) {
319	    job := &scheduler.Job{
320	        Name:     "test",
321	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *",
322	        Handler:  func(ctx context.Context) error { return nil },
323	    }
324	
325	    if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
326	        t.Fatalf("invalid job: %v", err)
327	    }
328	}
329	```
330	
331	## Comparison to Other Solutions
332	
333	| Feature | scheduler | robfig/cron | github.com/go-co-op/gocron |
334	|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|
335	| Standard cron syntax | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
336	| Seconds support | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
337	| Timezone support | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
338	| Middleware pattern | ✅ | ⚠️ (basic) | ❌ |
339	| Graceful shutdown | ✅ | ⚠️ (basic) | ✅ |
340	| Zero dependencies | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
341	| Job metadata | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ (limited) |
342	
343	## API Reference
344	
345	See [example_test.go](./example_test.go) for comprehensive examples.
346	
347	### Core Types
348	
349	- `Scheduler` - Manages scheduled jobs
350	- `Job` - Job definition with schedule and handler
351	- `Middleware` - Function that wraps job handlers
352	
353	### Functions
354	
355	- `New(opts ...Option) *Scheduler` - Create new scheduler
356	- `WithTimezone(tz string) Option` - Set default timezone
357	- `WithMiddleware(mw ...Middleware) Option` - Add middleware
358	
359	### Methods
360	
361	- `Register(job *Job) error` - Add job to scheduler
362	- `Start() error` - Begin executing jobs
363	- `Stop(ctx context.Context) error` - Graceful shutdown

13		jobs       map[string]*registeredJob
14		jobsMu     sync.RWMutex
15		timezone   *time.Location
16		middleware Middleware
17		running    bool
18		runningMu  sync.RWMutex
19		stopCh     chan struct{}
20		wg         sync.WaitGroup
21	}
22	
23	// registeredJob wraps a Job with runtime state.
24	type registeredJob struct {
25		job      *Job
26		cancelFn context.CancelFunc
27	}
28	
29	// Option configures a Scheduler.
30	type Option func(*Scheduler)
31	
32	// WithTimezone sets the default timezone for all jobs.
33	func WithTimezone(tz string) Option {
34		return func(s *Scheduler) {
35			loc, err := time.LoadLocation(tz)
36			if err != nil {
37				// Default to UTC on invalid timezone
38				loc = time.UTC
39			}
40			s.timezone = loc
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// WithMiddleware sets middleware to wrap all job handlers.
45	func WithMiddleware(mw ...Middleware) Option {
46		return func(s *Scheduler) {
47			if len(mw) > 0 {
48				s.middleware = Chain(mw...)
49			}
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// New creates a new Scheduler with optional configuration.
54	func New(opts ...Option) *Scheduler {
55		s := &Scheduler{
56			jobs:     make(map[string]*registeredJob),
57			timezone: time.UTC,
58			stopCh:   make(chan struct{}),
59		}
60	
61		for _, opt := range opts {
62			opt(s)
63		}
64	
65		return s
66	}
67	
68	// Register adds a job to the scheduler.
69	// Jobs must be registered before calling Start().
70	func (s *Scheduler) Register(job *Job) error {
71		if job == nil {
72			return errors.New("job cannot be nil")
73		}
74	
75		if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
76			return errors.Wrap(err, "invalid job")
77		}
78	
79		s.jobsMu.Lock()
80		defer s.jobsMu.Unlock()
81	
82		if _, exists := s.jobs[job.Name]; exists {
83			return errors.Errorf("job with name %q already registered", job.Name)
84		}
85	
86		s.jobs[job.Name] = &registeredJob{job: job}
87		return nil
88	}
89	
90	// Start begins executing scheduled jobs.
91	func (s *Scheduler) Start() error {
92		s.runningMu.Lock()
93		defer s.runningMu.Unlock()
94	
95		if s.running {
96			return errors.New("scheduler already running")
97		}
98	
99		s.jobsMu.RLock()
100		defer s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
101	
102		// Parse and schedule all jobs
103		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
104			schedule, err := ParseCronExpression(rj.job.Schedule)
105			if err != nil {
106				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to parse schedule for job %q", rj.job.Name)
107			}
108	
109			ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
110			rj.cancelFn = cancel
111	
112			s.wg.Add(1)
113			go s.runJobWithSchedule(ctx, rj, schedule)
114		}
115	
116		s.running = true
117		return nil
118	}
119	
120	// runJobWithSchedule executes a job according to its cron schedule.
121	func (s *Scheduler) runJobWithSchedule(ctx context.Context, rj *registeredJob, schedule *Schedule) {
122		defer s.wg.Done()
123	
124		// Apply middleware to handler
125		handler := rj.job.Handler
126		if s.middleware != nil {
127			handler = s.middleware(handler)
128		}
129	
130		for {
131			// Calculate next run time
132			now := time.Now()
133			if rj.job.Timezone != "" {
134				loc, err := time.LoadLocation(rj.job.Timezone)
135				if err == nil {
136					now = now.In(loc)
137				}
138			} else if s.timezone != nil {
139				now = now.In(s.timezone)
140			}
141	
142			next := schedule.Next(now)
143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)
146	
147			select {
148			case <-timer.C:
149				// Add job name to context and execute
150				jobCtx := withJobName(ctx, rj.job.Name)
151				if err := handler(jobCtx); err != nil {
152					// Error already handled by middleware (if any)
153					_ = err
154				}
155			case <-ctx.Done():
156				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
157				timer.Stop()
158				return
159			case <-s.stopCh:
160				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
161				timer.Stop()
162				return
163			}
164		}
165	}

167	// Stop gracefully shuts down the scheduler.
168	// It waits for all running jobs to complete or until the context is canceled.
169	func (s *Scheduler) Stop(ctx context.Context) error {
170		s.runningMu.Lock()
171		if !s.running {
172			s.runningMu.Unlock()
173			return errors.New("scheduler not running")
174		}
175		s.running = false
176		s.runningMu.Unlock()
177	
178		// Cancel all job contexts
179		s.jobsMu.RLock()
180		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
181			if rj.cancelFn != nil {
182				rj.cancelFn()
183			}
184		}
185		s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
186	
187		// Signal stop and wait for jobs to finish
188		close(s.stopCh)
189	
190		done := make(chan struct{})
191		go func() {
192			s.wg.Wait()
193			close(done)
194		}()
195	
196		select {
197		case <-done:
198			return nil
199		case <-ctx.Done():
200			return ctx.Err()
201		}
202	}

12	// Schedule represents a parsed cron expression.
13	type Schedule struct {
14		seconds  fieldMatcher // 0-59 (optional, for 6-field format)
15		minutes  fieldMatcher // 0-59
16		hours    fieldMatcher // 0-23
17		days     fieldMatcher // 1-31
18		months   fieldMatcher // 1-12
19		weekdays fieldMatcher // 0-7 (0 and 7 are Sunday)
20		hasSecs  bool
21	}
22	
23	// fieldMatcher determines if a field value matches.
24	type fieldMatcher interface {
25		matches(value int) bool
26	}

28	// ParseCronExpression parses a cron expression and returns a Schedule.
29	// Supports both 5-field (minute hour day month weekday) and 6-field (second minute hour day month weekday) formats.
30	func ParseCronExpression(expr string) (*Schedule, error) {
31		if expr == "" {
32			return nil, errors.New("empty cron expression")
33		}
34	
35		fields := strings.Fields(expr)
36		if len(fields) != 5 && len(fields) != 6 {
37			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid cron expression: expected 5 or 6 fields, got %d", len(fields))
38		}
39	
40		s := &Schedule{
41			hasSecs: len(fields) == 6,
42		}
43	
44		var err error
45		offset := 0
46	
47		// Parse seconds (if 6-field format)
48		if s.hasSecs {
49			s.seconds, err = parseField(fields[0], 0, 59)
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid seconds field")
52			}
53			offset = 1
54		} else {

56		}

58		// Parse minutes
59		s.minutes, err = parseField(fields[offset], 0, 59)
60		if err != nil {

62		}

64		// Parse hours
65		s.hours, err = parseField(fields[offset+1], 0, 23)

68		}

72		if err != nil {

74		}

115	
116		// Should never reach here with valid cron expressions
117		return time.Time{}
118	}
119	
120	// matches checks if the given time matches the schedule.
121	func (s *Schedule) matches(t time.Time) bool {
122		return s.seconds.matches(t.Second()) &&
123			s.minutes.matches(t.Minute()) &&
124			s.hours.matches(t.Hour()) &&
125			s.months.matches(int(t.Month())) &&
126			(s.days.matches(t.Day()) || s.weekdays.matches(int(t.Weekday())))
127	}
128	
129	// parseField parses a single cron field (supports *, ranges, lists, steps).
130	func parseField(field string, min, max int) (fieldMatcher, error) {
131		// Wildcard
132		if field == "*" {
133			return &wildcardMatcher{}, nil
134		}
135	
136		// Step values (*/N)
137		if strings.HasPrefix(field, "*/") {
138			step, err := strconv.Atoi(field[2:])
139			if err != nil || step < 1 || step > max {
140				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid step value: %s", field)
141			}
142			return &stepMatcher{step: step, min: min, max: max}, nil
143		}
144	
145		// List (1,2,3)
146		if strings.Contains(field, ",") {
147			parts := strings.Split(field, ",")
148			values := make([]int, 0, len(parts))
149			for _, p := range parts {
150				val, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(p))
151				if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
152					return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid list value: %s", p)
153				}
154				values = append(values, val)
155			}
156			return &listMatcher{values: values}, nil
157		}
158	
159		// Range (1-5)
160		if strings.Contains(field, "-") {
161			parts := strings.Split(field, "-")
162			if len(parts) != 2 {
163				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
164			}
165			start, err1 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
166			end, err2 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
167			if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || start < min || end > max || start > end {
168				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
169			}
170			return &rangeMatcher{start: start, end: end}, nil
171		}
172	
173		// Exact value
174		val, err := strconv.Atoi(field)
175		if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
176			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid value: %s (must be between %d and %d)", field, min, max)
177		}
178		return &exactMatcher{value: val}, nil
179	}
180	
181	// wildcardMatcher matches any value.
182	type wildcardMatcher struct{}
183	
184	func (*wildcardMatcher) matches(_ int) bool {
185		return true
186	}
187	
188	// exactMatcher matches a specific value.
189	type exactMatcher struct {
190		value int
191	}
192	
193	func (m *exactMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
194		return value == m.value
195	}
196	
197	// rangeMatcher matches values in a range.
198	type rangeMatcher struct {
199		start, end int
200	}
201	
202	func (m *rangeMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
203		return value >= m.start && value <= m.end
204	}
205	
206	// listMatcher matches any value in a list.
207	type listMatcher struct {
208		values []int
209	}
210	
211	func (m *listMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
212		return slices.Contains(m.values, value)
213	}
214	
215	// stepMatcher matches values at regular intervals.
216	type stepMatcher struct {
217		step, min, max int
218	}
219	
220	func (m *stepMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
221		if value < m.min || value > m.max {
222			return false
223		}
224		return (value-m.min)%m.step == 0
225	}

11	// Middleware wraps a JobHandler to add cross-cutting behavior.
12	type Middleware func(JobHandler) JobHandler
13	
14	// Chain combines multiple middleware into a single middleware.
15	// Middleware are applied in the order they're provided (left to right).
16	func Chain(middlewares ...Middleware) Middleware {
17		return func(handler JobHandler) JobHandler {
18			// Apply middleware in reverse order so first middleware wraps outermost
19			for _, middleware := range slices.Backward(middlewares) {
20				handler = middleware(handler)
21			}
22			return handler
23		}
24	}
25	
26	// Recovery recovers from panics in job handlers and converts them to errors.
27	func Recovery(onPanic func(jobName string, recovered interface{})) Middleware {
28		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
29			return func(ctx context.Context) (err error) {
30				defer func() {
31					if r := recover(); r != nil {
32						jobName := getJobName(ctx)
33						if onPanic != nil {
34							onPanic(jobName, r)
35						}
36						err = errors.Errorf("job %q panicked: %v", jobName, r)
37					}
38				}()
39				return next(ctx)
40			}
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// Logger is a minimal logging interface.
45	type Logger interface {
46		Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
47		Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
48	}
49	
50	// Logging adds execution logging to jobs.
51	func Logging(logger Logger) Middleware {
52		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
53			return func(ctx context.Context) error {
54				jobName := getJobName(ctx)
55				start := time.Now()
56	
57				logger.Info("Job started", "job", jobName)
58	
59				err := next(ctx)
60				duration := time.Since(start)
61	
62				if err != nil {
63					logger.Error("Job failed", "job", jobName, "duration", duration, "error", err)
64				} else {
65					logger.Info("Job completed", "job", jobName, "duration", duration)
66				}
67	
68				return err
69			}
70		}
71	}
72	
73	// Timeout wraps a job handler with a timeout.
74	func Timeout(duration time.Duration) Middleware {
75		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
76			return func(ctx context.Context) error {
77				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, duration)
78				defer cancel()
79	
80				done := make(chan error, 1)
81				go func() {
82					done <- next(ctx)
83				}()
84	
85				select {
86				case err := <-done:
87					return err
88				case <-ctx.Done():
89					return errors.Errorf("job %q timed out after %v", getJobName(ctx), duration)
90				}
91			}
92		}
93	}

112		return "unknown"

3	A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.

5	## Features
6	
7	- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
8	- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
9	- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
10	- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
11	- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
12	- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
13	- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage

15	## Installation
16	
17	This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.

19	## Quick Start
20	
21	```go
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25	    "context"
26	    "fmt"
27	    "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"
28	)
29	
30	func main() {
31	    s := scheduler.New()
32	
33	    s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
34	        Name:     "daily-cleanup",
35	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
36	        Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
37	            fmt.Println("Running cleanup...")
38	            return nil
39	        },
40	    })
41	
42	    s.Start()
43	    defer s.Stop(context.Background())
44	
45	    // Keep running...
46	    select {}
47	}
48	```

50	## Cron Expression Format
51	
52	### 5-Field Format (Standard)
53	```
54	┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
55	│ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
56	│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
57	│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
58	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7) (Sunday = 0 or 7)
59	│ │ │ │ │
60	* * * * *
61	```
62	
63	### 6-Field Format (With Seconds)
64	```
65	┌───────────── second (0 - 59)
66	│ ┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
67	│ │ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
68	│ │ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
69	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
70	│ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7)
71	│ │ │ │ │ │
72	* * * * * *
73	```
74	
75	### Special Characters
76	
77	- `*` - Any value (every minute, every hour, etc.)
78	- `,` - List of values: `1,15,30` (1st, 15th, and 30th)
79	- `-` - Range: `9-17` (9 AM through 5 PM)
80	- `/` - Step: `*/15` (every 15 units)
81	
82	### Common Examples
83	
84	| Schedule | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `* * * * *` | Every minute |
87	| `0 * * * *` | Every hour |
88	| `0 0 * * *` | Daily at midnight |
89	| `0 9 * * 1-5` | Weekdays at 9 AM |
90	| `*/15 * * * *` | Every 15 minutes |
91	| `0 0 1 * *` | First day of every month |
92	| `0 0 * * 0` | Every Sunday at midnight |
93	| `30 14 * * *` | Every day at 2:30 PM |
94	
95	## Timezone Support
96	
97	```go
98	// Global timezone for all jobs
99	s := scheduler.New(
100	    scheduler.WithTimezone("America/New_York"),
101	)
102	
103	// Per-job timezone (overrides global)
104	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
105	    Name:     "tokyo-report",
106	    Schedule: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM Tokyo time
107	    Timezone: "Asia/Tokyo",
108	    Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
109	        // Runs at 9 AM in Tokyo
110	        return nil
111	    },
112	})
113	```
114	
115	**Important**: Always use IANA timezone names (`America/New_York`, not `EST`).

117	## Middleware
118	
119	Middleware wraps job handlers to add cross-cutting behavior. Multiple middleware can be chained together.
120	
121	### Built-in Middleware
122	
123	#### Recovery (Panic Handling)
124	
125	```go
126	s := scheduler.New(
127	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
128	        scheduler.Recovery(func(jobName string, r interface{}) {
129	            log.Printf("Job %s panicked: %v", jobName, r)
130	        }),
131	    ),
132	)
133	```
134	
135	#### Logging
136	
137	```go
138	type Logger interface {
139	    Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
140	    Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
141	}
142	
143	s := scheduler.New(
144	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
145	        scheduler.Logging(myLogger),
146	    ),
147	)
148	```
149	
150	#### Timeout
151	
152	```go
153	s := scheduler.New(
154	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
155	        scheduler.Timeout(5 * time.Minute),
156	    ),
157	)
158	```
159	
160	### Combining Middleware
161	
162	```go
163	s := scheduler.New(
164	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
165	        scheduler.Recovery(panicHandler),
166	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
167	        scheduler.Timeout(10 * time.Minute),
168	    ),
169	)
170	```
171	
172	**Order matters**: Middleware are applied left-to-right. In the example above:
173	1. Recovery (outermost) catches panics from everything
174	2. Logging logs the execution
175	3. Timeout (innermost) wraps the actual handler
176	
177	### Custom Middleware
178	
179	```go
180	func Metrics(recorder MetricsRecorder) scheduler.Middleware {
181	    return func(next scheduler.JobHandler) scheduler.JobHandler {
182	        return func(ctx context.Context) error {
183	            start := time.Now()
184	            err := next(ctx)
185	            duration := time.Since(start)
186	
187	            jobName := scheduler.GetJobName(ctx)
188	            recorder.Record(jobName, duration, err)
189	
190	            return err
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	```

196	## Graceful Shutdown
197	
198	Always use `Stop()` with a context to allow jobs to finish cleanly:
199	
200	```go
201	// Give jobs up to 30 seconds to complete
202	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
203	defer cancel()
204	
205	if err := s.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
206	    log.Printf("Shutdown error: %v", err)
207	}
208	```
209	
210	Jobs should respect context cancellation:
211	
212	```go
213	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
214	    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
215	        select {
216	        case <-ctx.Done():
217	            return ctx.Err() // Canceled
218	        default:
219	            // Do work
220	        }
221	    }
222	    return nil
223	}
224	```

226	## Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Always Name Your Jobs
229	
230	Names are used for logging, metrics, and debugging:
231	
232	```go
233	Name: "user-cleanup-job" // Good
234	Name: "job1"             // Bad
235	```
236	
237	### 2. Add Descriptions and Tags
238	
239	```go
240	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
241	    Name:        "stale-session-cleanup",
242	    Description: "Removes user sessions older than 30 days",
243	    Tags:        []string{"maintenance", "security"},
244	    Schedule:    "0 3 * * *",
245	    Handler:     cleanupSessions,
246	})
247	```
248	
249	### 3. Use Appropriate Middleware
250	
251	Always include Recovery and Logging in production:
252	
253	```go
254	scheduler.New(
255	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
256	        scheduler.Recovery(logPanic),
257	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
258	    ),
259	)
260	```
261	
262	### 4. Avoid Scheduling Exactly on the Hour
263	
264	Many systems schedule jobs at `:00`, causing load spikes. Stagger your jobs:
265	
266	```go
267	"5 2 * * *"  // 2:05 AM (good)
268	"0 2 * * *"  // 2:00 AM (often overloaded)
269	```
270	
271	### 5. Make Jobs Idempotent
272	
273	Jobs may run multiple times (crash recovery, etc.). Design them to be safely re-runnable:
274	
275	```go
276	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
277	    // Use unique constraint or check-before-insert
278	    db.Exec("INSERT IGNORE INTO processed_items ...")
279	    return nil
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 6. Handle Timezones Explicitly
284	
285	Always specify timezone for business-hour jobs:
286	
287	```go
288	Timezone: "America/New_York" // Good
289	// Timezone: ""              // Bad (defaults to UTC)
290	```
291	
292	### 7. Test Your Cron Expressions
293	
294	Use a cron expression calculator before deploying:
295	- [crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru/)
296	- Write unit tests with the parser
297

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {

11	// Scheduler manages scheduled jobs.
12	type Scheduler struct {
13		jobs       map[string]*registeredJob
14		jobsMu     sync.RWMutex
15		timezone   *time.Location
16		middleware Middleware
17		running    bool
18		runningMu  sync.RWMutex
19		stopCh     chan struct{}
20		wg         sync.WaitGroup
21	}
22	
23	// registeredJob wraps a Job with runtime state.
24	type registeredJob struct {
25		job      *Job
26		cancelFn context.CancelFunc
27	}
28	
29	// Option configures a Scheduler.
30	type Option func(*Scheduler)
31	
32	// WithTimezone sets the default timezone for all jobs.
33	func WithTimezone(tz string) Option {
34		return func(s *Scheduler) {
35			loc, err := time.LoadLocation(tz)
36			if err != nil {
37				// Default to UTC on invalid timezone
38				loc = time.UTC
39			}
40			s.timezone = loc
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// WithMiddleware sets middleware to wrap all job handlers.
45	func WithMiddleware(mw ...Middleware) Option {
46		return func(s *Scheduler) {
47			if len(mw) > 0 {
48				s.middleware = Chain(mw...)
49			}
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// New creates a new Scheduler with optional configuration.
54	func New(opts ...Option) *Scheduler {
55		s := &Scheduler{
56			jobs:     make(map[string]*registeredJob),
57			timezone: time.UTC,
58			stopCh:   make(chan struct{}),
59		}
60	
61		for _, opt := range opts {
62			opt(s)
63		}
64	
65		return s
66	}
67	
68	// Register adds a job to the scheduler.
69	// Jobs must be registered before calling Start().
70	func (s *Scheduler) Register(job *Job) error {
71		if job == nil {
72			return errors.New("job cannot be nil")
73		}
74	
75		if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
76			return errors.Wrap(err, "invalid job")
77		}
78	
79		s.jobsMu.Lock()
80		defer s.jobsMu.Unlock()
81	
82		if _, exists := s.jobs[job.Name]; exists {
83			return errors.Errorf("job with name %q already registered", job.Name)
84		}
85	
86		s.jobs[job.Name] = &registeredJob{job: job}
87		return nil
88	}
89	
90	// Start begins executing scheduled jobs.
91	func (s *Scheduler) Start() error {
92		s.runningMu.Lock()
93		defer s.runningMu.Unlock()
94	
95		if s.running {
96			return errors.New("scheduler already running")
97		}
98	
99		s.jobsMu.RLock()
100		defer s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
101	
102		// Parse and schedule all jobs
103		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
104			schedule, err := ParseCronExpression(rj.job.Schedule)
105			if err != nil {
106				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to parse schedule for job %q", rj.job.Name)
107			}
108	
109			ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
110			rj.cancelFn = cancel
111	
112			s.wg.Add(1)
113			go s.runJobWithSchedule(ctx, rj, schedule)
114		}
115	
116		s.running = true
117		return nil
118	}

120	// runJobWithSchedule executes a job according to its cron schedule.
121	func (s *Scheduler) runJobWithSchedule(ctx context.Context, rj *registeredJob, schedule *Schedule) {

138			} else if s.timezone != nil {

3	import (

12	// Schedule represents a parsed cron expression.
13	type Schedule struct {
14		seconds  fieldMatcher // 0-59 (optional, for 6-field format)
15		minutes  fieldMatcher // 0-59
16		hours    fieldMatcher // 0-23
17		days     fieldMatcher // 1-31
18		months   fieldMatcher // 1-12
19		weekdays fieldMatcher // 0-7 (0 and 7 are Sunday)
20		hasSecs  bool
21	}
22	
23	// fieldMatcher determines if a field value matches.
24	type fieldMatcher interface {
25		matches(value int) bool
26	}
27	
28	// ParseCronExpression parses a cron expression and returns a Schedule.
29	// Supports both 5-field (minute hour day month weekday) and 6-field (second minute hour day month weekday) formats.
30	func ParseCronExpression(expr string) (*Schedule, error) {
31		if expr == "" {
32			return nil, errors.New("empty cron expression")
33		}
34	
35		fields := strings.Fields(expr)
36		if len(fields) != 5 && len(fields) != 6 {
37			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid cron expression: expected 5 or 6 fields, got %d", len(fields))
38		}
39	
40		s := &Schedule{
41			hasSecs: len(fields) == 6,
42		}
43	
44		var err error
45		offset := 0
46	
47		// Parse seconds (if 6-field format)
48		if s.hasSecs {
49			s.seconds, err = parseField(fields[0], 0, 59)
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid seconds field")
52			}
53			offset = 1
54		} else {
55			s.seconds = &exactMatcher{value: 0} // Default to 0 seconds
56		}
57	
58		// Parse minutes
59		s.minutes, err = parseField(fields[offset], 0, 59)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid minutes field")
62		}
63	
64		// Parse hours
65		s.hours, err = parseField(fields[offset+1], 0, 23)
66		if err != nil {
67			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid hours field")
68		}
69	
70		// Parse days
71		s.days, err = parseField(fields[offset+2], 1, 31)
72		if err != nil {
73			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid days field")
74		}
75	
76		// Parse months
77		s.months, err = parseField(fields[offset+3], 1, 12)
78		if err != nil {
79			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid months field")
80		}
81	
82		// Parse weekdays (0-7, where both 0 and 7 represent Sunday)
83		s.weekdays, err = parseField(fields[offset+4], 0, 7)
84		if err != nil {
85			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid weekdays field")
86		}
87	
88		return s, nil
89	}

91	// Next returns the next time the schedule should run after the given time.
92	func (s *Schedule) Next(from time.Time) time.Time {
93		// Start from the next second/minute
94		if s.hasSecs {
95			from = from.Add(1 * time.Second).Truncate(time.Second)
96		} else {
97			from = from.Add(1 * time.Minute).Truncate(time.Minute)
98		}
99	
100		// Cap search at 4 years to prevent infinite loops
101		maxTime := from.AddDate(4, 0, 0)
102	
103		for from.Before(maxTime) {
104			if s.matches(from) {
105				return from
106			}
107	
108			// Advance to next potential match
109			if s.hasSecs {
110				from = from.Add(1 * time.Second)
111			} else {
112				from = from.Add(1 * time.Minute)
113			}
114		}
115	
116		// Should never reach here with valid cron expressions
117		return time.Time{}
118	}

120	// matches checks if the given time matches the schedule.
121	func (s *Schedule) matches(t time.Time) bool {
122		return s.seconds.matches(t.Second()) &&
123			s.minutes.matches(t.Minute()) &&
124			s.hours.matches(t.Hour()) &&
125			s.months.matches(int(t.Month())) &&
126			(s.days.matches(t.Day()) || s.weekdays.matches(int(t.Weekday())))
127	}

129	// parseField parses a single cron field (supports *, ranges, lists, steps).
130	func parseField(field string, min, max int) (fieldMatcher, error) {
131		// Wildcard
132		if field == "*" {
133			return &wildcardMatcher{}, nil
134		}
135	
136		// Step values (*/N)
137		if strings.HasPrefix(field, "*/") {
138			step, err := strconv.Atoi(field[2:])
139			if err != nil || step < 1 || step > max {
140				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid step value: %s", field)
141			}
142			return &stepMatcher{step: step, min: min, max: max}, nil
143		}
144	
145		// List (1,2,3)
146		if strings.Contains(field, ",") {
147			parts := strings.Split(field, ",")
148			values := make([]int, 0, len(parts))
149			for _, p := range parts {
150				val, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(p))
151				if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
152					return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid list value: %s", p)
153				}
154				values = append(values, val)
155			}
156			return &listMatcher{values: values}, nil
157		}
158	
159		// Range (1-5)
160		if strings.Contains(field, "-") {
161			parts := strings.Split(field, "-")
162			if len(parts) != 2 {
163				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
164			}
165			start, err1 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
166			end, err2 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
167			if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || start < min || end > max || start > end {
168				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
169			}
170			return &rangeMatcher{start: start, end: end}, nil
171		}
172	
173		// Exact value
174		val, err := strconv.Atoi(field)
175		if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
176			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid value: %s (must be between %d and %d)", field, min, max)
177		}
178		return &exactMatcher{value: val}, nil
179	}

181	// wildcardMatcher matches any value.
182	type wildcardMatcher struct{}
183	
184	func (*wildcardMatcher) matches(_ int) bool {
185		return true
186	}

188	// exactMatcher matches a specific value.
189	type exactMatcher struct {
190		value int
191	}
192	
193	func (m *exactMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
194		return value == m.value
195	}

197	// rangeMatcher matches values in a range.
198	type rangeMatcher struct {
199		start, end int
200	}
201	
202	func (m *rangeMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
203		return value >= m.start && value <= m.end
204	}
205	
206	// listMatcher matches any value in a list.
207	type listMatcher struct {
208		values []int
209	}
210	
211	func (m *listMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
212		return slices.Contains(m.values, value)
213	}
214	
215	// stepMatcher matches values at regular intervals.
216	type stepMatcher struct {
217		step, min, max int
218	}
219	
220	func (m *stepMatcher) matches(value int) bool {
221		if value < m.min || value > m.max {
222			return false
223		}
224		return (value-m.min)%m.step == 0
225	}

11	// Middleware wraps a JobHandler to add cross-cutting behavior.
12	type Middleware func(JobHandler) JobHandler
13	
14	// Chain combines multiple middleware into a single middleware.
15	// Middleware are applied in the order they're provided (left to right).
16	func Chain(middlewares ...Middleware) Middleware {
17		return func(handler JobHandler) JobHandler {
18			// Apply middleware in reverse order so first middleware wraps outermost
19			for _, middleware := range slices.Backward(middlewares) {
20				handler = middleware(handler)
21			}
22			return handler
23		}
24	}
25	
26	// Recovery recovers from panics in job handlers and converts them to errors.
27	func Recovery(onPanic func(jobName string, recovered interface{})) Middleware {
28		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
29			return func(ctx context.Context) (err error) {
30				defer func() {
31					if r := recover(); r != nil {
32						jobName := getJobName(ctx)
33						if onPanic != nil {
34							onPanic(jobName, r)
35						}
36						err = errors.Errorf("job %q panicked: %v", jobName, r)
37					}
38				}()
39				return next(ctx)
40			}
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// Logger is a minimal logging interface.
45	type Logger interface {
46		Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
47		Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
48	}
49	
50	// Logging adds execution logging to jobs.
51	func Logging(logger Logger) Middleware {
52		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
53			return func(ctx context.Context) error {
54				jobName := getJobName(ctx)
55				start := time.Now()
56	
57				logger.Info("Job started", "job", jobName)
58	
59				err := next(ctx)
60				duration := time.Since(start)
61	
62				if err != nil {
63					logger.Error("Job failed", "job", jobName, "duration", duration, "error", err)
64				} else {
65					logger.Info("Job completed", "job", jobName, "duration", duration)
66				}
67	
68				return err
69			}
70		}
71	}
72	
73	// Timeout wraps a job handler with a timeout.
74	func Timeout(duration time.Duration) Middleware {
75		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
76			return func(ctx context.Context) error {
77				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, duration)
78				defer cancel()
79	
80				done := make(chan error, 1)
81				go func() {
82					done <- next(ctx)
83				}()
84	
85				select {
86				case err := <-done:
87					return err
88				case <-ctx.Done():
89					return errors.Errorf("job %q timed out after %v", getJobName(ctx), duration)
90				}
91			}
92		}
93	}

2	
3	A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.
4	
5	## Features
6	
7	- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
8	- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
9	- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
10	- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
11	- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
12	- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
13	- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage
14	
15	## Installation
16	
17	This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	```go
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25	    "context"
26	    "fmt"
27	    "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"
28	)
29	
30	func main() {
31	    s := scheduler.New()
32	
33	    s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
34	        Name:     "daily-cleanup",
35	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
36	        Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
37	            fmt.Println("Running cleanup...")
38	            return nil
39	        },
40	    })
41	
42	    s.Start()
43	    defer s.Stop(context.Background())
44	
45	    // Keep running...
46	    select {}
47	}
48	```

50	## Cron Expression Format
51	
52	### 5-Field Format (Standard)
53	```
54	┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
55	│ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
56	│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
57	│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
58	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7) (Sunday = 0 or 7)
59	│ │ │ │ │
60	* * * * *
61	```
62	
63	### 6-Field Format (With Seconds)
64	```
65	┌───────────── second (0 - 59)
66	│ ┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
67	│ │ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
68	│ │ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
69	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
70	│ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7)
71	│ │ │ │ │ │
72	* * * * * *
73	```
74	
75	### Special Characters
76	
77	- `*` - Any value (every minute, every hour, etc.)
78	- `,` - List of values: `1,15,30` (1st, 15th, and 30th)
79	- `-` - Range: `9-17` (9 AM through 5 PM)
80	- `/` - Step: `*/15` (every 15 units)
81	
82	### Common Examples
83	
84	| Schedule | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `* * * * *` | Every minute |
87	| `0 * * * *` | Every hour |
88	| `0 0 * * *` | Daily at midnight |
89	| `0 9 * * 1-5` | Weekdays at 9 AM |
90	| `*/15 * * * *` | Every 15 minutes |
91	| `0 0 1 * *` | First day of every month |
92	| `0 0 * * 0` | Every Sunday at midnight |
93	| `30 14 * * *` | Every day at 2:30 PM |
94	
95	## Timezone Support
96	
97	```go
98	// Global timezone for all jobs
99	s := scheduler.New(
100	    scheduler.WithTimezone("America/New_York"),
101	)
102	
103	// Per-job timezone (overrides global)
104	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
105	    Name:     "tokyo-report",
106	    Schedule: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM Tokyo time
107	    Timezone: "Asia/Tokyo",
108	    Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
109	        // Runs at 9 AM in Tokyo
110	        return nil
111	    },
112	})
113	```
114	
115	**Important**: Always use IANA timezone names (`America/New_York`, not `EST`).
116	
117	## Middleware
118	
119	Middleware wraps job handlers to add cross-cutting behavior. Multiple middleware can be chained together.
120	
121	### Built-in Middleware
122	
123	#### Recovery (Panic Handling)
124	
125	```go
126	s := scheduler.New(
127	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
128	        scheduler.Recovery(func(jobName string, r interface{}) {
129	            log.Printf("Job %s panicked: %v", jobName, r)
130	        }),
131	    ),
132	)
133	```
134	
135	#### Logging
136	
137	```go
138	type Logger interface {
139	    Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
140	    Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
141	}
142	
143	s := scheduler.New(
144	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
145	        scheduler.Logging(myLogger),
146	    ),
147	)
148	```
149	
150	#### Timeout
151	
152	```go
153	s := scheduler.New(
154	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
155	        scheduler.Timeout(5 * time.Minute),
156	    ),
157	)
158	```
159	
160	### Combining Middleware
161	
162	```go
163	s := scheduler.New(
164	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
165	        scheduler.Recovery(panicHandler),
166	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
167	        scheduler.Timeout(10 * time.Minute),
168	    ),
169	)
170	```
171	
172	**Order matters**: Middleware are applied left-to-right. In the example above:
173	1. Recovery (outermost) catches panics from everything
174	2. Logging logs the execution
175	3. Timeout (innermost) wraps the actual handler
176	
177	### Custom Middleware
178	
179	```go
180	func Metrics(recorder MetricsRecorder) scheduler.Middleware {
181	    return func(next scheduler.JobHandler) scheduler.JobHandler {
182	        return func(ctx context.Context) error {
183	            start := time.Now()
184	            err := next(ctx)
185	            duration := time.Since(start)
186	
187	            jobName := scheduler.GetJobName(ctx)
188	            recorder.Record(jobName, duration, err)
189	
190	            return err
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	```

196	## Graceful Shutdown
197	
198	Always use `Stop()` with a context to allow jobs to finish cleanly:
199	
200	```go
201	// Give jobs up to 30 seconds to complete
202	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
203	defer cancel()
204	
205	if err := s.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
206	    log.Printf("Shutdown error: %v", err)
207	}
208	```
209	
210	Jobs should respect context cancellation:
211	
212	```go
213	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
214	    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
215	        select {
216	        case <-ctx.Done():
217	            return ctx.Err() // Canceled
218	        default:
219	            // Do work
220	        }
221	    }
222	    return nil
223	}
224	```

226	## Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Always Name Your Jobs
229	
230	Names are used for logging, metrics, and debugging:
231	
232	```go
233	Name: "user-cleanup-job" // Good
234	Name: "job1"             // Bad
235	```
236	
237	### 2. Add Descriptions and Tags
238	
239	```go
240	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
241	    Name:        "stale-session-cleanup",
242	    Description: "Removes user sessions older than 30 days",
243	    Tags:        []string{"maintenance", "security"},
244	    Schedule:    "0 3 * * *",
245	    Handler:     cleanupSessions,
246	})
247	```
248	
249	### 3. Use Appropriate Middleware
250	
251	Always include Recovery and Logging in production:
252	
253	```go
254	scheduler.New(
255	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
256	        scheduler.Recovery(logPanic),
257	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
258	    ),
259	)
260	```
261	
262	### 4. Avoid Scheduling Exactly on the Hour
263	
264	Many systems schedule jobs at `:00`, causing load spikes. Stagger your jobs:
265	
266	```go
267	"5 2 * * *"  // 2:05 AM (good)
268	"0 2 * * *"  // 2:00 AM (often overloaded)
269	```
270	
271	### 5. Make Jobs Idempotent
272	
273	Jobs may run multiple times (crash recovery, etc.). Design them to be safely re-runnable:
274	
275	```go
276	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
277	    // Use unique constraint or check-before-insert
278	    db.Exec("INSERT IGNORE INTO processed_items ...")
279	    return nil
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 6. Handle Timezones Explicitly
284	
285	Always specify timezone for business-hour jobs:
286	
287	```go
288	Timezone: "America/New_York" // Good
289	// Timezone: ""              // Bad (defaults to UTC)
290	```
291	
292	### 7. Test Your Cron Expressions
293	
294	Use a cron expression calculator before deploying:
295	- [crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru/)
296	- Write unit tests with the parser
297
